chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We were in Al-Bayda' at the end of the night, so I performed ablution and brushed my teeth, while I was intending to pray. Then it was as if something entered my heart, so can one pray in Al-Bayda' in the carriage?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not pray in Al-Bayda'. I said: 'And where is the boundary of Al-Bayda'?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when he reached Dhat Al-Jaysh, would hasten in travel, then he would not pray until he arrived at the encampment of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). I said: 'And where is Dhat Al-Jaysh?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Before Al-Hafira, by three miles'.

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءِ: The open desert or empty land
key_terms.الْحَفِيرَةِ: Al-Hafira, a well or location near Medina
key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: The carriage or howdah used for travel
key_terms.ذَاتَ الْجَيْشِ: Dhat Al-Jaysh, a place near Medina

ai.seo_question: Where is the boundary of Al-Bayda' and is it permissible to pray there while traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith delineates the specific legal boundary of 'Al-Bayda'—a region near Medina where prayer was historically disliked due to pre-Islamic superstitions or impurity—by anchoring the ruling to the practical precedent of Imam al-Baqir (AS). By defining the limit as three miles before Al-Hafira, the text provides a precise geographical criterion for travelers to determine when to resume full, preferred prayer conditions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' lived experiences to interpret abstract legal concepts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘We were in Al-Bayda’a at the end of the night. So I performed ablution and brushed my teeth, and I worried about the Salāt. Then it was as if something entered into my heart. So can one pray Salāt in Al-Bayda’a in the carriage?’ So heasws said: ‘You cannot pray Salāt in Al-Bayda’a’. I said, ‘And where is the boundary of Al-Bayda’a?’ So heasws said: ‘It was so that whenever Abu Ja’farasws reached Zaat Al-Jaysh, would travel faster. Then heasws would not pray Salāt until he came over to Muarras of the Prophetsaww’. I said, ‘And where is Zaat Al-Jaysh?’ So heasws said: ‘Besides Al-Hafira, by three miles’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘We were in al-Bayda’ (name of a place) toward the end of the night. I took Wudu’, brushed my teeth and I intended to perform Salah (prayer), then it occurred to me. Is it permissible to perform Salah (prayer), in al-Bayda’ in the carriage? He (the Imam) said, ‘Do not perform Salah (prayer) in al-Bayda’.’ I then asked, ‘What are the limits of al- Bayda’?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would on reaching Dhat al-Jaysh travel faster. He (the Imam) would not perform Salah (prayer) until reaching Mu‘arras of the Holy prophet.’ I then asked, ‘Where is Dhat al-Jaysh?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is three miles before al-Hafirah.’”
